title: Implement temporally-weighted regression fence and quorum rollforward for canaries
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a temporally-weighted canary regression fence with quorum-based rollforward/backstop behavior. Improves sensitivity for gradual regressions while reducing noise from transient bursts; exposes operator knobs in Console and new metrics for monitoring.
description:
Motivation: some regressions we see (long-tail growth, slow drift) are not well-captured by single-window detectors and often flip-flop due to bursty traffic. This PR introduces a temporally-weighted regression fence (TWRF) that fuses metric signals across time with exponential decay weights, combined with a traffic-slice quorum evaluator that makes decisions across independent cohorts (region, customer tier, model-route). The goal is to catch gradual degradations with high confidence while avoiding false positives from short-lived spikes.

What this change does (summary):
- Adds a temporally-weighted metric fusion module (server/runtimes/canary/twrf) that maintains an exponentially decaying summary of per-metric deltas (p50/p95/p99/throughput/error-rate).
- Implements a quorum-based evaluator which checks whether a configurable fraction of active traffic slices exceed significance thresholds for a configurable sustained window.
- Introduces a rollforward/backstop policy: when quorum confirms improvement, canary weight is eligible for accelerated increase (rollforward); when quorum detects sustained regression, traffic is throttled back and an automatic backstop route to stable model is applied.
- Exposes Console-facing knobs: decay_half_life_ms, quorum_fraction, sustain_window_seconds, backstop_weight_floor, rollforward_acceleration_factor.
- Adds observability: new metrics (canary.twrf.score, canary.quorum.count, canary.backstop.triggered, canary.rollforward.rate) and dashboards.

Design details:
- Temporal fusion uses exponential decay per-slice: score_t = alpha * delta_t + (1-alpha) * score_{t-1}, where alpha is derived from decay_half_life_ms and event spacing. This keeps sensitivity to recent changes while preserving memory of gradual trends.
- Per-slice significance uses bootstrap-derived thresholds (baseline distribution captured during warmup). We compute standardized deltas to make thresholds comparable across metrics.
- Quorum logic evaluates the fraction of slices with sustained significant deltas over sustain_window_seconds and requires quorum_fraction to be met for an action. Quorum is resilient to noisy / low-traffic slices (we ignore slices below a traffic floor).
- Rollforward/backstop policies are implemented as policy plugins in the routing layer; backstop is conservative (drops canary weight toward backstop_weight_floor and routes excess traffic to base model variant); rollforward uses a capped exponential increase controlled by rollforward_acceleration_factor and a cooldown.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for temporal fusion math, quorum evaluator, and plugin hooks (tests/runtimes/canary/twrf_test.go).
- Integration test in perf-canary harness simulating gradual drift and bursty noise; asserts low false positive rate and timely detection of sustained regressions.
- Manual staging run with 10% canary on staging cluster for 24h collecting canary.twrf.score and quorum traces.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Feature gated by config flag canary.enable_twrf (off by default). We will ship with flag off and enable for internal perf sweeps.
- Enable monitoring dashboards and create an alert that fires when canary.backstop.triggered > 0 in production for > 1 occurrence/week.
- After 2 weeks of internal validation we will enable opt-in in Console for customers under canary experiments.

Related: ENG-3174 (algorithm spec), ENG-3190 (Console knobs), SUP-4421 (customer-reported slow drift incident).

Notes: this PR focuses on canary decision logic and instrumentation. It does not change core model runtime kernels or batching logic. It is designed to interoperate with existing synthetic probe detectors and the sentinel rollback guard; we intentionally implemented rollforward as a symmetric policy next to rollback to support both safe recovery and cautious progression.
